note: Re-judged 2026-11-03 by an independent auditor who authored none of 816ce1ce4c, 2cbd255ba4, 2e5c2d012a, d22b811ce4 or 1a2ccaeef8 (phase 5 of spec-filter-wire-0-umbrella, the per-peer text filter chain deleted). RFC 2545 Section 3 read: "In all other cases a BGP speaker shall advertise to its peer in the Network Address field only the global IPv6 address of the next hop (the value of the Length of Network Address of Next Hop field shall be set to 16)." The one moved unit, TestRFC2545ForwardPolicyOwnGlobalJointSubnet, changed only the filter plumbing: The test filter is now an answerTransport behind filterTransportSeam, compiled by answerPolicy into a policychain library chain, so the verdict travels the real filter-update path (route.Input, rpc.FilterUpdateOutput decoded by the library chain) instead of the deleted policyFilterSeam that handed a PolicyResponse straight to the text chain; that is the production path every plugin filter now takes. Its assertions are byte-identical: the recipient-off-link output is exactly the 16-octet own global with length 0x10 and the common-link output keeps the pair, on cached and rs, so an always-append or never-append producer goes red. Other carriers unmoved; their judgement stands. Ran the tagged units under ./le job run at HEAD (-tags ze_bgp, -v): PASS (scratch audit-p5-units-v.log). Verdict unchanged: enforced.
